pages.title: Cabins
pages.content:
Twelve self-catering cabins in four sizes: Fern sleeps 2, Beech sleeps 4, Cedar sleeps 6 and Hollow sleeps 8. Every cabin has its own kitchen, porch and wood stove, and every stay is two nights or more.

Prices per night: Fern €140, Beech €190, Cedar €260, Hollow €360. They include linen, towels, the first basket of firewood and final cleaning. A longer comparison of the four sizes comes with the full Cabins page.

pages.title: Inside
pages.content: The same plain comforts in every cabin: a wood stove with split firewood, an induction hob and oven, a fridge, a kettle and a coffee press, crockery for the number of beds, linen and towels, a rain shower and a porch with two chairs. There are no televisions.

pages.title: The Forest
pages.content: Thirty-eight hectares of mixed cedar and beech woodland, with three marked walks: the Short loop (2.4 km, 45 minutes), the Beech ridge (5.8 km, 2 hours) and the River path (8.1 km, 3 hours).

pages.title: Reserve
pages.content:
There is one way to hold a weekend: choose a cabin and dates, send a hold request, and we keep the cabin for 48 hours while we confirm with a 30% deposit link. Free cancellation until 14 days before arrival.

Write to stay@komorebi-cabins.example with the cabin, your dates, how many of you are coming and a phone number.

pages.title: About
pages.content: Komorebi Cabins was founded in 2014 by Ilse Marten and Ruben Okafor on thirty-eight hectares of cedar and beech woodland in Hollin Vale. The first four cabins opened that summer, eight more followed in 2017, and the woodshed office was added in 2022.

pages.title: People
pages.content: Seven people look after the village: Ilse Marten, Ruben Okafor, Sofia Navarro, Amira Haddad, Tobias Klein, Nora Adeyemi and Jonah Pereira.

pages.title: Getting here
pages.content: Larch Gate, Gravel Lane, Hollin Vale. By car the last 400 metres are gravel, with parking beside each cabin. By train, take the service to Hollin Vale station, then bus 32 to Larch Gate and a ten-minute walk.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content: Write to stay@komorebi-cabins.example or call +44 1632 960 418 between 08:30 and 19:00 every day. We reply within one working day.

pages.title: The Woodshed Letter
pages.content: One short note on the first Thursday of each month: the weekends still open, the season in the woods and one recipe for the cabin stove.

pages.title: Legal and Privacy
pages.content: This site stores nothing about you beyond what WordPress needs to run. Emails you send to the village are used only to answer you.

posts.title: Stacking wood for October
posts.excerpt: Why the cedar goes at the back of the porch stack and the beech at the front.
posts.content:
By the second week of October the porches begin to fill. Ruben splits the cedar in the summer, when it dries fastest, and the beech in the spring, when it is still easy to work. Each cabin gets a stack of roughly two baskets against its north wall, with the cedar at the back for kindling and the beech at the front for the long burn.

Every morning at ten the firewood round reaches every porch. Guests rarely see it happen: a basket appears, the old one is taken, and the stack is squared off again. It is the quietest job in the village and the one people mention most in the visitor book.

If you are arriving in October, bring a warm layer for the evenings and leave the stove to the first basket. A cabin heated slowly with beech feels very different from one heated quickly with cedar, and we are happy to show you how.

posts.title: Why Friday check-in starts at three
posts.excerpt: The four hours between check-out and check-in, and what happens in them.
posts.content:
Check-out is at eleven and check-in is at three, and the four hours between are the most carefully planned of the week. Sofia and her team strip, wash and air every cabin, open the windows for an hour, and lay the stove with fresh kindling before the beds are made.

We have tried shorter gaps. A cabin turned in two hours is clean but it does not smell of the woods, and the first thing guests tell us they notice on arrival is the smell. Four hours is what it takes for the airing to finish.

So if you reach Hollin Vale early, the woodshed office is open from half past eight and there is a bench on the porch with a view of the lane. The kettle is always on.

posts.title: The beech that fell in March
posts.excerpt: A storm brought down a hundred-year-old beech beside the River path. This is what we did with it.
posts.content:
In the last week of March a storm brought down a beech that had stood beside the River path for more than a century. It missed the nearest cabin by a few metres and left a clearing the size of a small field.

Jonah closed the path for two days while Ruben and Tobias cut the trunk into lengths. The straight sections went to the carpentry shed, where they will become benches for the porches. The rest was split and stacked, and it will heat the stoves this coming winter.

The clearing is already filling with light and, by June, with ferns. The walk is open again, and the stump is the best seat on the river path.
